payload.wikitext: {{Short description|Genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = [[Late Cretaceous]], {{fossilrange|Campanian|Campanian|[[Campanian]]}} | image = Plesiolophus skull reconstruction.jpg | image_caption = Hypothetical skull reconstruction of ''Plesiolophus'' | display_parents = 2 | genus = Plesiolophus | parent_authority = McFeeters et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = warnerensis | authority = McFeeters et al., 2026 }} '''''Plesiolophus''''' ({{lit|near crest}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[lambeosaurine]] [[hadrosaurid]] dinosaur known from the [[Late Cretaceous]] ([[Campanian]] age) [[Oldman Formation]] of Canada. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Plesiolophus warnerensis''''', known from a partial skull. It belongs to the clade Parasaurolophini, where it exhibits more primitive cranial characters than its relatives. == Discovery and naming == The ''Plesiolophus'' fossil material was discovered by [[Wendy Sloboda]] in the outcrops of the [[Oldman Formation]], part of the [[Belly River Group]], near Warner, [[Alberta]], Canada. The specimen is housed in the [[Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen TMP 2016.023.0039. It consists of a partial skull, including the posterior [[skull roof]] and [[braincase]]. [[File:Plesiolophus warnerensis.png|thumb|left|[[Life restoration]]]] In 2026, Bradley D. McFeeters and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Plesiolophus warnerensis'' as a new genus and species of hadrosaurid dinosaur based on these fossil remains, establishing TMP 2016.023.0039 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Plesiolophus'', combines the [[Ancient Greek]] words {{lang|grc|πλησ´ιoν}}, meaning {{gloss|near}}, and {{lang|grc|λόϕoς}}, meaning {{gloss|crest}}, in reference to the phylogenetic proximity of this taxon to ''[[Parasaurolophus]]'', but its retention of more [[plesiomorphic]] ('primitive') anatomy. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''warnerensis'', references the discovery of the specimen in Warner, Alberta. == Classification == To test the affinities and relationships of ''Plesiolophus'', McFeeters et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Ramírez Velasco (2022). Their strict consensus tree, which obtained better-resolved results, recovered the Asian ''[[Charonosaurus]]'' as the earliest-diverging member of the [[lambeosaurine]] clade Parasaurolophini. It is followed by an exclusively North American clade, of which ''Plesiolophus'' is the [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basalmost]] member.
